title: How Digital Product Payment Solutions in West Africa Works and How to Deploy It Today
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling digital products from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Zimbabwe is fully operational with sovereign commerce infrastructure that has no geographic restrictions.
imageAlt: Digital creator in Ghana building a sovereign store with crypto payments and NOWPayments
imageCaption: The blockchain has no geographic restrictions — a wallet in Lagos processes identically to one in London.

content.text: In Nigeria, Ghana, and other West African countries, digital creators face significant hurdles in selling their products online due to platform restrictions and payment limitations. Stripe and PayPal are often unavailable, leaving creators without a reliable way to collect payments. This is where sovereign digital commerce infrastructure comes in, providing a solution that bypasses these restrictions and enables creators to sell their products globally.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to this infrastructure's success lies in its use of blockchain-based payments, such as USDT on Tron, which settles in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10. This allows creators to receive payments from international buyers without relying on traditional payment platforms. Additionally, the use of Cloudflare infrastructure ensures that the digital product store is highly available and secure, making it an attractive solution for creators who want to sell their products online.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your sovereign digital commerce stack, you'll need to have a few things in place. First, you'll need to choose a blockchain-based payment method, such as NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies. You'll also need to set up a digital wallet to receive payments. Finally, you'll need to create a Cloudflare account to host your digital product store and configure your payment and delivery pipeline.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up your payment and delivery pipeline is a straightforward process. You'll need to integrate your blockchain-based payment method with your digital product store, using a service like NOWPayments to handle payment verification. You'll also need to configure your digital product delivery system, using a service like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to store and deliver your digital products. With these systems in place, you'll be able to receive payments and deliver products to your customers automatically.
Sovereign digital commerce infrastructure bypasses traditional payment platforms, enabling creators to sell digital products globally.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you're ready to go live and process your first transaction. This is an exciting moment, as you'll be able to see your sovereign digital commerce stack in action. To process your first transaction, simply send a test payment to your digital wallet and verify that it's been received. Then, deliver a digital product to a test customer to ensure that your delivery system is working correctly.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your sovereign digital commerce stack is up and running, you can start to scale your business. This might involve adding more digital products to your store, expanding your marketing efforts, or optimizing your payment and delivery pipeline for better performance. With a scalable infrastructure in place, you'll be able to handle increasing demand and grow your business quickly and efficiently.

To sell digital products to international buyers, creators in Africa can use a sovereign digital commerce stack that bypasses traditional payment platforms. This stack uses blockchain-based payments, such as USDT on Tron, to receive payments from buyers worldwide.
